data.narrative:
Duranium is a pre-seed stage company in Climate & Energy founded by Berkley Noble and Brenden Prins-McKinney, having raised $2M+. The sector comp universe includes one public company (LNZA) and eight private peers, among them Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable valuation method here. Using the $2M total raised as a proxy for current enterprise value and applying a standard 2.5x step-up multiplier for pre-seed to next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $5M. This reflects typical capital efficiency expectations at early stage. Peer-median triangulation is not applicable; while nine same-sector peers exist in the Climate & Energy space, none meet the narrow filter criteria of matching stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier—a minimum of three datapoints is required to avoid misleading extrapolation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $4M to $6M, centered on a $5M median. This single-method output carries meaningful uncertainty: the lack of tight peer comparables at pre-seed stage in this sector limits cross-validation. Key sensitivities include the founders' track record, technical differentiation within climate tech, and capital efficiency relative to sector norms, none of which are quantified in available data. A second triangulation method would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
